newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge up on local demand.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge up on local demand.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged up on Wednesday in early trade on local demand and traders forecast the growth would continue all day.
The Russian Trading System 23-share index edged up to 327.52 at the opening from Tuesday's closing 327.37.
At 1050 GMT utility Kolenergo KOLE.RTS rose to $0.290 from $0.278 at Tuesday's close, Rostelekom RTKM.RTS was $4.12 after $4.10, and LUKoil LKOH.RTS edged up to $14.56 from $14.38.
"The market is most likely to grow, the trend is quite good, although we cannot rule out a small correction which we see every day," Troika Dialog chief trader Alexei Dolgikh said.
But the price rise is mainly supported by Russian buying on small trade volumes, traders said.
"I cannot see big orders today, mainly rouble purchases,"said United City Bank chief trader Samit Yakovlev.
Traders said Tuesday's price rise on news of Anatoly Chubais's appointment as First Deputy Prime Minister was due to local operators. Western demand was quiet and only in some shares.
The market shrugged off President Boris Yeltsin's decree on Tuesday about a full government reshuffle.
"I think the West will react more to new government actions, not the new people," Yakovlev said.
